entries.title: Jump to the brand kit from any surface it drives
entries.summary: A palette icon now appears next to every design surface that reads from a **Brand kit** — the event page builder, system email designer, title slide designer (**Colours** panel, next to **Reset to brand**), clip export editor (**Renders**), and the Create carousel toolbar (when a kit is selected). Clicking the icon opens the exact kit the design uses in a new tab, so unsaved work in the editor is not lost. Hovering or focusing the icon shows a tooltip listing which kit assets — logo, colour swatches, fonts, tagline, hashtags or clip caption style — that surface actually pulls from.
entries.use_case: When an organizer notices a colour or font looks off in a slide, clip or email design, they can click the palette icon to jump straight to the brand kit driving that design — without hunting through menus — and fix the source asset in one step.

cs_action.note: Ships automatically for all customers with Brand kit access (limited_release). No configuration needed.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer asks how to keep slides, clips and emails visually consistent, or when they struggle to find which kit is driving a particular design.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers actively using Brand kits with Slides, Clips, or Create carousels.
internal.staff_path: Marketing → Brand → any kit; or open a slide/clip/carousel/page-builder design and look for the palette icon
internal.gotchas: The link is intentionally absent from booklets, Advocacy Quick Launch and Advocacy video templates — those surfaces do not read the Marketing brand kit, so the link would point at irrelevant assets. Webinar share cards and email signatures are also not yet wired (coming in a follow-up branch).
internal.talk_track: Every design surface that uses your brand kit now has a palette icon that takes you straight to that kit in a new tab — so you can check or update the source without losing your place in the editor.

draft.docs_gap: The brand-kits guide should add a section listing every surface that displays the palette shortcut icon and explaining that the tooltip shows which specific kit assets (logo, colours, fonts, voice, clips) that surface reads.
draft.why_use_it: Brand kits let you define your event's logo, colours, fonts, voice and content rules in one place so every marketing surface — slides, clips, carousels, page builder and system emails — stays visually consistent without manual updates. When a kit changes, every surface that reads from it reflects the update automatically. Use a brand kit whenever you want a team of contributors to produce on-brand content without coordinating design decisions individually.

entries.title: Report a subsession's parent session fields on the same row
entries.summary: The Report Builder has a **Parent session** group of fields, labelled **Parent Session …** so their columns are easy to tell apart. On a subsession row it adds the session's own values — **Format**, **Track**, **Level**, **Language**, **Room**, **Status**, **Submitter**, **Title**, **Description**, its other standard fields and its custom fields — next to the subsession and its participants. Each subsession has one parent, so the report gains no extra rows, and you can filter and sort on these fields. Before, a subsession row only showed the session's title and IDs; its Format, Track and custom fields came from the subsession itself, which is usually blank.

where.path: Reports → Report Builder → Fields → Parent session

entries.use_case: A program team that collects presentations as subsessions needs one roster with the session's format, track, submitter and description next to every presenter — for a program book, a disclosure review or a CME export — without matching two spreadsheets on Session ID.

cs_action.note: ASA (ANESTHESIOLOGY 2027 / ADVANCE 2028) asked for this (HubSpot ticket 50511758943, SB-11095); build or update their subsession submission report with the Parent session fields. Any customer using subsessions with format/track on the parent benefits.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer reports blank Format or Track columns on a subsession report, duplicate rows on a session report with subsession columns, or exports two reports to match in Excel.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers who collect presentations, abstracts or talks as subsessions under a parent session (medical and scientific meetings especially).
internal.staff_path: Event → Reports → open or create a Sessions report → Fields → Parent session
internal.gotchas: Parent session fields are empty on a session's own row — filter Is Subsession is Yes. Restricted (record-scoped) team roles can use the fields on a Sessions report but cannot pick Parent session as the report's main subject.
internal.talk_track: Subsession reports can now carry the session's format, track, submitter, description and custom fields on every row, so one report replaces matching two exports.

entries.title: Report Builder shows descriptions and other rich text as readable text
entries.summary:
Rich-text fields — session **Description**, speaker **Biography**, group and task descriptions, and custom **Rich Text** or **Text Area** fields — now come back as readable text in the Report Builder preview and in CSV and Excel downloads, instead of editor HTML like `

…

`. Paragraphs, line breaks and list items stay on separate lines; filters still match the text as stored. Dashboards, share links and Ask return the same text.
entries.use_case: An organizer exporting session descriptions for a program book or a CME submission gets clean text they can paste, without stripping HTML tags in Excel.

cs_action.note: Applies to every report automatically. ASA reported it (HubSpot 50511758943, SB-11086).

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer says descriptions or bios in a report or export are full of tags.
internal.who_should_get_it: Everyone who reports on descriptions, bios or rich-text custom fields.
internal.staff_path: Event → Reports → any Sessions report → add Description → preview or Download
internal.gotchas: Formatting (bold, links) is not kept — the export is plain text. Saved reports pick this up without changes.
internal.talk_track: Descriptions and bios now export as clean text, with paragraphs and list items on their own lines.

entries.title: Number fields keep leading zeros, such as member IDs
entries.summary: A **Number** field now keeps a value exactly as typed, so a member ID like **0755092** keeps its leading zero when it is edited on a contact, in a grid cell, in Bulk Edit, on a submission or portal form, or filled in from a membership lookup. Before, a new contact kept the zero but any later edit saved 755092. The contacts grid and reports show the ID as stored. Values still sort, filter and add up as numbers.
entries.use_case: Associations that store member or customer IDs with leading zeros in a Number field can match them to their CRM without the IDs changing on edit.

cs_action.note: ASA (SB-11093): 274 ASA IDs lost their zero before the fix; Josh runs the repair after ASA confirms IDs are 7 digits. Other orgs with leading-zero numbers in US: 7 (182 values), EU: 2 (383).

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer says IDs in a Number field lose a leading zero, or match inconsistently to their CRM.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers storing member, customer or NPI-style IDs in Number fields.
internal.staff_path: Event → Contacts → a contact → a Number custom field
internal.gotchas: Values that already lost the zero are not changed by the fix; they need a repair (retype, or a staff SQL fix). Opening a CSV directly in Excel still drops leading zeros (Excel does that) — use the Excel download. Still numeric, so still zero-less: the Public API returns Number values as numbers, and the legacy module exports and email merge tags print through the value-types package (parseFloat) until that package is released.
internal.talk_track: Number fields now keep IDs exactly as you type them, leading zeros included.

entries.title: Live Transcribe lists each session participant once
entries.summary: The **Participants** card on a session in the **Live Transcribe Console** lists each person once, under the session role they hold. Before, a participant with a custom role such as **Panelist** also appeared a second time as **Speaker**.

where.path: Live Transcribe Console → a session → Participants

entries.use_case: An AV crew or producer checking who is on stage sees the real panel line-up once, with each person's role, instead of a doubled list that looks like extra speakers.

cs_action.note: Automatic for every Live Transcribe event. Reported by Clarion / Infocast (SB-11085); prod had 18,442 sessions in 78 US events with the duplicate rows.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer reports a Panelist, Moderator or other custom-role participant listed twice, once as Speaker, in Live Transcribe.
internal.who_should_get_it: Live Transcribe customers whose sessions use custom participant roles (panels, moderated sessions).
internal.staff_path: Event → Marketing → Transcribe → Invites → open the Console link → a session → Participants
internal.gotchas: Display fix only; the underlying participant data did not change.
internal.talk_track: The Participants card now shows the panel as it really is, one line per person under their role.

entries.title: Tagged speaker names show wherever a transcript is read
entries.summary: Once you tag a voice on a recording or Live Transcribe session, the person's name replaces the "Speaker 4" placeholder in transcript search results, **Ask** answers, chapters, session recaps and the **Attend** app's session recap. A generic tag such as "Audience Member 2" shows its label. A participant whose seat on the session is hidden is never named, and names that come from the recording platform (Zoom, Goldcast) are kept.

where.path: Marketing → Media → a recording → Speakers → Tag

entries.use_case: A marketing team that tags speakers once gets recaps, chapters and search results that credit the right person by name, without re-importing the recording or fixing names by hand.

cs_action.note: Automatic, read-time: existing tags apply immediately with no re-import (SB-10990, API side).

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer says recaps, search results or Ask answers say "Speaker 4" even though the speakers were tagged.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers using Live Transcribe or Media with speaker tagging.
internal.staff_path: Event → Marketing → Media → a recording → Speakers → Tag; then search the transcript or regenerate a recap
internal.gotchas: Already-generated recaps and stored quotes keep the placeholder until regenerated / re-extracted; clip chat and home search do not resolve tags yet. Brand Voice examples also match tagged names now (limited release, not in the public summary). Create's speaker credit and citation tooltip are a separate entry (create-speaker-attribution) that needs web-ui-v2#1457 in production.
internal.talk_track: Tag a speaker once and their name follows the transcript everywhere it is used.

entries.title: Forms on a trial event show a Trial mode banner and don't take submissions
entries.summary: While an organization or event is on a trial, its public forms show a **Trial mode** banner. Submitters can fill in a form and **Save as draft**, but **Submit** and payment are off, on call for papers forms and on the event website's award, request, reviewer, registration and RSVP forms. Everything opens as soon as the trial ends.

where.path: Public call for papers forms and event website pages of a trial organization or event

entries.use_case: A team setting up its event before the contract is signed can build, share and test its forms without collecting real submissions or payments by accident.

cs_action.note: Trial is a staff flag on the org or event. Before a trial customer opens a call for papers, nominations or registration, staff must turn trial off for the org and the event, or every final submit and payment is refused (403 trial_mode). Drafts and admin previews still work.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When onboarding a customer on a trial, and whenever a customer reports "Trial mode" on a live form or that submitters can't press Submit or Pay.
internal.who_should_get_it: Organizations or events Sessionboard has put on a trial (pre-contract or pre-renewal).
internal.staff_path: Staff only: turn off trial on the organization and on the event; the banner and the block clear at once (nothing is cached).
internal.gotchas: A trial flag on the org blocks every event's public forms, and a trial flag on any event behind an org Site form blocks that form. Check both flags. At ship time US had 3 trial orgs and 7 trial events, EU 1 trial event; confirm none is live and collecting.
internal.talk_track: While you set up on a trial, your forms are a safe preview: people can try them and save drafts, and submissions and payments open the moment your account is live.

entries.title: Large session lists load faster: subsessions load when you expand a parent
entries.summary: On **Program → Sessions** and the agenda's **List** tab, a parent session's subsessions now load when you expand it, with a short **Loading…** row, instead of arriving with every page. When you search, a parent that matches only through its subsessions shows just the matching ones, already expanded, as filters already did. Pages of events with thousands of subsessions load in a fraction of the time.
entries.use_case: A program team running an event with hundreds of subsessions under a few parents can page, search and filter the Sessions list quickly instead of waiting on, or timing out on, every subsession at once.

cs_action.note: Automatic. Came out of the 2026-11-04 prod-us outage (SB-11108): CES 2027 (205 parents, 6,226 subsessions) list pages were 2-12 MB and OOM-killed API tasks; customers saw "CORS Error: Unable to reach the API".

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer with many subsessions reports a slow Sessions or agenda list, or a "CORS Error: Unable to reach the API" while paging it.
internal.who_should_get_it: Events with large numbers of subsessions (abstract-driven medical and scientific meetings, CES-style programs).
internal.staff_path: Event → Program → Sessions → expand a parent session
internal.gotchas: Exports, reports and the calendar still carry every subsession; only the list grid loads them on expand. A parent loads its subsessions once per list load; editing a row refreshes that row only.
internal.talk_track: Big programs page instantly now; a session's subsessions load when you open it.
